title: Fundamental theorem of calculus for a Lipschitz curve with continuous a.e. derivative
statement: Let l >= 0, phi, k : R -> R^l, a <= b real and L >= 0. Suppose phi is L-Lipschitz on [a, b], k is continuous on [a, b], and for Lebesgue-almost every t in the open interval (a, b) the map phi has derivative k(t) at t. Then phi(b) - phi(a) = integral_a^b k(t) dt.
lean_statement: ∀ (ℓ : ℕ) (φ k : ℝ → Rn ℓ) (a b : ℝ) (L : ℝ≥0), a ≤ b → LipschitzOnWith L φ (Icc a b) → ContinuousOn k (Icc a b) → (∀ᵐ t ∂(volume : Measure ℝ), t ∈ Ioo a b → HasDerivAt φ (k t) t) → φ b - φ a = ∫ t in a..b, k t
